ai.title: Pass costMode through subagent context
ai.summary: Added optional `costMode` string to `SubagentContextParams` and passed it through in `extractSubagentContextParams` in `spawn-agent-utils.ts`. Ensures subagents inherit the correct cost mode from the parent session context. Internal type and logic change in agent-runtime package.

eli5.text: The assistant can now pass its current pricing setting to helper agents it spins off, so those helpers stay on the same billing mode as the main session. You wouldn't notice this directly, but it keeps subagents from accidentally using a different cost mode than the one you're working under.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.619 release
ai.summary: Version 1.0.619 of the Freebuff CLI is released, updating the package version in cli/release/package.json from 1.0.618. This is a release-bump commit that packages the surrounding day's work: the costMode subagent context propagation in the agent-runtime package, the code-reviewer-lite free agent mapping to minimax/minimax-m2.5, the Ctrl+U debug logging cleanup in the multiline input component, test alignment fixes in local-agents.test.ts and messages.test.ts, and the buffbench eval switching its base2 target to base2-free. The CLI binary distribution is rebuilt with these accumulated changes.
ai.evidence: Modified cli/release/package.json: version field bumped from 1.0.618 to 1.0.619 in the codebuff package manifest only, with no other file changes in the commit.

eli5.text: This release of the Freebuff CLI adds a new free code-review assistant and makes sub-agents more reliable by passing along your session settings, plus it tidies up the terminal input experience. You can now try a lightweight code-review assistant right away because it has been added to the free agent list and connects to a capable AI model. When you spawn helper sub-agents, they now inherit your cost-mode setting so they behave consistently with your main session instead of defaulting to an unexpected mode. The multiline text input no longer spams debug logs when you clear a line with Ctrl+U, keeping the terminal output cleaner while typing. On top of these user-facing improvements, the bundled test suite and evaluation harness were corrected so future changes stay more accurate and stable.

ai.title: commander-lite model swap to grok-4.1-fast
ai.summary: commander-lite agent model set updated from minimax/minimax-m2.5 to x-ai/grok-4.1-fast in common/src/constants/free-agents.ts. Ensures free mode command execution matches correct model routing. Scope limited to shared core constants affecting free agent configuration.

eli5.text: When you run a command in free mode (the lightweight assistant that helps with basic tasks), it now uses a different AI model called grok-4.1-fast instead of minimax-m2.5. This swap only affects the 'commander-lite' feature, which is the tool responsible for executing commands in free mode, and it ensures that it routes to the correct model for handling those commands. If you use free mode and trigger a command run, you might notice slightly different output style or performance, but the core functionality remains the same. The change is live today, as it updates a shared configuration used by the free mode system.

ai.title: Add skillsDir parameter to SDK client and run state
ai.summary: Introduced `skillsDir` parameter in `CodebuffClientOptions` and `InitialSessionStateOptions`. This allows custom skill loading paths to override default locations in `sdk/src/client.ts` and `sdk/src/run-state.ts`. The change propagates through `run.ts` and `index.ts` to support isolated skill directories.

eli5.text: If you run the assistant from your own software using the toolkit, you can now tell it to load custom skills from a folder you choose instead of the default locations. The toolkit passes that folder path through to where skills are gathered, so any skill placed in your chosen directory will appear in the assistant's skill list and be ready to use. This is already live in today's toolkit version.

ai.title: SDK 0.10.6 adds skillsDir parameter
ai.summary: SDK 0.10.6 introduces `skillsDir` parameter for custom skill directory loading. Mechanism: allows explicit path specification for skill discovery. Scope: `@codebuff/sdk` package, `sdk/CHANGELOG.md`. Detail: New parameter added to SDK configuration options.

eli5.text: The assistant's helper tools can now be stored in a custom folder instead of only the default one. If you looked, you would see an extra setting where you type the address of your own folder, and the assistant would go look there for its skills. This change is live today for anyone using the helper toolkit in their own project.

ai.title: SDK version bump to 0.10.6
ai.summary: Bumps @codebuff/sdk package version from 0.10.5 to 0.10.6 in sdk/package.json. This is a standard version increment for the official Codebuff SDK.

eli5.text: If you use Codebuff's developer kit to build tools on top of the platform, your software now runs against the updated library version that bundles recent fixes and new capabilities released over the past week. These include a rewritten rendering layer that stops cutting off text in wide tables by wrapping it instead, a corrected abort path so partially generated answers flush cleanly when you stop a response mid-stream, and the ability for the free mode to skip the old editor-lite helper and apply code edits directly before calling in a code-reviewer-lite instance for a second pass. New CLI agents named commander-lite and code-reviewer-lite are selectable in free mode, and the feedback you send from the command line now travels to a new endpoint so your reports reach the team's dashboard instead of staying on your machine. Anyone importing Codebuff's API today gets these behaviors automatically; older integrations that pin to the previous version number will need to move to the new one to pick them up.

ai.title: Pricing hero tooltip clarifies mode and limit scope
ai.summary: Pricing hero copy updated to 'Subscribe to use all modes with higher usage limits' with a HelpCircle tooltip explaining 'Includes 5-hour sessions with weekly limits'. Hero container padding shifted from py-8 to pb-12 for layout balance. Tooltip components imported from @/components/ui/tooltip. Scope limited to web/src/app/pricing/pricing-client.tsx.

eli5.text: The text on the subscription page now reads 'Subscribe to use all modes with higher usage limits', and a small question-mark icon next to it opens a brief note saying the plan comes with 5-hour sessions and weekly limits. The only other difference is that the spacing above the rest of the page content changed slightly so things look a bit more balanced. These tweaks are live today for anyone looking at the pricing page.
